headings.guidance: Explain purpose, intended users, supported document/output types and scope in 250–350 words. Do not add architecture, interface or testing subsections here; those have their own requested sections.

Explain actual modules and responsibilities, and two concrete end-to-end workflows including entry point, transformation and output. Distinguish observed calls from inferred runtime success. Focus on implementation, not a repeated product introduction.

Describe actual CLI commands/flags or API routes, configuration fields, inputs, outputs, dependency/runtime prerequisites, and specific validation/error behavior. Use an optional compact table when useful. Never invent HTTP endpoints for a CLI.

Describe test functions and CI steps that appear in the supplied source, explicitly without claiming they were run. Propose a short acceptance checklist with exact actions and expected outcomes. Summarize actual limitations; do not demand unrelated production metrics.

guidance: Write a practical, source-grounded technical overview. Keep section scopes distinct: overview explains purpose and users; architecture explains implementation and workflows; interfaces describes commands or APIs and dependencies; verification describes actual test code and proposed checks. Do not repeat an introduction or a full architecture in every section. Demonstration data in repository examples is not the application being documented. Statements about error recovery require a visible error-handling branch, not just a template with TODO markers.
